reason: The core algebra is correct and I reproduced it independently: (i) the score, block inverse Q^{-1}e_4=D^{-1}(-gamma,1), phi, zeta_b, alpha_{b,j} and the A1 per-r identity all check (the Fraction brute force in a1_exact_check is exact, and I re-derived each step by hand); (ii) an independent Monte Carlo of the ACTUAL sampling sd of sqrt(n)*b_hat with my own corrected-score implementation (n=4000, 1500 reps) gives ratio to the formula 1.006+-0.018 (wide, m=128), 1.019+-0.018 (wide, unclipped g), 0.981+-0.018 (narrow, m=128), 0.970+-0.018 (wide, m=32) - i.e. the formula is the true asymptotic variance, not merely what HC1/CR1 estimate; (iii) D, gamma, w_1, the sup and the m-budgets in the claim match a1_exact_check.out / a1b_largen_and_budget.json; Omega is PSD (eigenvalues checked) and a dense 2-D grid over {osc<=2} confirms the sup at (-8,8) in all three worlds at m=32,128. Two defects remain, so the claim AS STATED is not proved. (1) Stated assumptions do not suffice. The claim lists only E[eta|r,t,K]=0 and Var(eta|r)=sigma^2(r); the derivation (1.5) silently uses eta independent of K given (r,t). The eta-term is E[E[eta^2|r,t,K](t-gamma'u)^2], so the formula needs E[eta^2|r,t,K]=sigma^2(r). Exact counterexample (Fractions, instance 1 of a1 with Var(eta|r,K)=sigma^2(r)(1+0.9(U_1(K)-r)), which keeps Var(eta|r)=sigma^2 and E[eta|r,t,K]=0): true [Q^{-1}BQ^{-1}]_44 / formula = 1.007806 at m=8 and 1.001411 at m=32 (exact inequality). In the Beta worlds the discrepancy is -0.55%/+0.55% of Var_1 at narrow m=32 and <=0.07% at m=128 - practically negligible, and the physical two-arm design satisfies the stronger condition by construction, but the assumption list must say so. (2) The uniform-in-g statement is overstated in scope. It conditions on sigma^2<=r(1-r)/8, which holds only without clipping, i.e. only for |g(r)|<=2min(r,1-r) on the support - a far smaller class than {|g|<=1} in the wide world: the claimed maximiser g*=1-8r+8r^2 clips 56-59% of wide-world prefixes (both arms, both sides), and with clipping sigma^2 is NOT <= r(1-r)/8 (r=0.02: 0.0154 vs 0.0025). Searching the admissible (b0,b1,b2) with the physical clipped sigma^2 in the wide world: the eta-component exceeds its 'bound' at g=1-4.8r+4.8r^2 (4.97e-3 vs 4.83e-3 at m=32; 4.92e-3 vs 4.78e-3 at m=128; 4.91e-3 vs 4.77e-3 at m=512), and the TOTAL sup is breached once the g-term is small: at m=4096 the physical max E[phi^2]=4.967e-3 > claimed sup 4.928e-3 (+0.8% variance). At m=32-512 the total sup still holds numerically only because the g-term at (-8,8) dominates (physical max = 0.85-0.94 of sup), not by the stated argument. Under clipping the mean is also misspecified (plim b_type = +0.0034 at g*, 0.0004-0.0006 at the claim's g in wide; negligible vs se but nonzero). Minor: derivation 1.6 says the alpha'V^{(4)}alpha term has degree <=7; alpha_{2,4}^2 V_44 and alpha_{2,2}^2 V_22 have degree 8 (conclusion 'moments <=8' unaffected; for linear g only moments <=6 are needed); 'law identified by its moments <=8' is an unnecessary restriction (only existence of moments is used); the clip fractions printed by a1b are not reported but 11%/4.5% of wide prefixes clip at g=0.18-0.8r (the simulation clips correctly, hence the 1.000-1.004 ratios are genuine). Everything disclaimed (finite-sample n=200, heavy tails at m=32, non-PD rate) is correctly outside the claim.
fix: (a) Replace 'Var(eta|r)=sigma^2(r)' in the assumptions by 'E[eta^2|r,t,K]=sigma^2(r) (e.g. eta independent of K given (r,t), true for independent Delta-arms and sel counts given r)'; the exact check and all numbers then stand. (b) State the uniform-in-g result over the no-clipping class G_phys={g:|g(r)|<=2min(r,1-r) on supp F_t} (equivalently add 'q_± in [0,1] a.s.' to the hypotheses), or, if {|g|<=1} is wanted, replace the eta bound by the clipped-arm variance sigma^2_clip(r)=[q+(1-q+)+q-(1-q-)]/16 with q±=clip(r±g/2) and take the sup jointly over (b0,b1,b2) - in the wide world this raises the eta-component by ~3% and breaches the current sup at large m (m>=4096, +0.8% variance); also record that under clipping the polynomial mean is misspecified (plim bias of b_type ~3e-3 at g*). (c) Correct derivation 1.6: g-term degree is 8 (alpha_{2,4}^2 V_44, alpha_{2,2}^2 V_22), so 'the A1 bound 8 is attained' holds for any beta_2 != 0, while linear g needs only moments <=6. (d) Drop 'identified by its moments <=8' from the scope; the formula needs only the existence of moments <=8 (automatic on [0,1]). (e) Report the clipping rate of the simulated worlds next to the 1.000-1.007 production ratios (wide: 11.0% type 0, 4.5% type 1 at g=0.18-0.8r).
strongest_attack_tried: Heteroskedastic-in-K error: exact Fraction enumeration with Var(eta|r,K)=sigma^2(r)(1+c(U_1(K)-r)), which satisfies every listed assumption (E[eta|r,t,K]=0, Var(eta|r)=sigma^2(r)) yet makes the true first-order variance differ from the closed form (ratio 1.0078 at m=8, 1.0014 at m=32; <=0.55% in the Beta worlds). Second attack: the physical clipped response model over the class {|g|<=1} - grid search over (b0,b1,b2) with true clipped sigma^2 shows the eta-bound sigma^2<=r(1-r)/8 fails pointwise and in integral (by ~3%) in the wide world, and the total sup is exceeded at m=4096; verified by an independent MC at g* (empirical sqrt(n)sd 0.369+-0.009 vs sup 0.418 at m=128, so at moderate m the sup still holds numerically). Also tried: independent MC of the true sampling sd vs formula (passes), dense 2-D brute force of the sup (passes), exact singular/point-mass worlds (correctly excluded by D>0), clustering with shared risks (first-order B unchanged, claim survives).
